_meta.purpose: Spec 35 Task 2 — the CLUSTER member sets (Text / Fill / Layout / Position / Motion) that make the element-manifest CLUSTER-COHERENCE rule computable. Expanded from three to six clusters per FR-35-2, then `flow` was merged back into `layout` the same day — see note_on_layout_merge. Five clusters.
_meta.source: Derived from setting-registry.json's css-property rows (golden master, 60 rows), grouped per the cluster table in .claude/plans/2026-07-20-spec-35-cluster-vocabulary-rework-design.md (FR-35-2). Every member.key below is a real setting_key in setting-registry.json — this file adds the missing CLUSTER axis + the default attr-suffix candidates the conformance checker uses to resolve a member to a block attribute (or a native `supports` path) when a block doesn't declare an explicit attrMap.
_meta.note_on_suffixes: `suffixes` are candidate PascalCase attribute-name suffixes tried in order against `{elementPrefix}{suffix}` when the element manifest has no explicit attrMap entry for that member. `nativeSupportsPath` (where present) is an ADDITIONAL resolution path: if the block's block.json `supports` object has a truthy value at that dot-path, the member counts as satisfied via WordPress-native supports (e.g. `spacing.padding`, `__experimentalBorder.radius`) even with no matching flat attribute — this is the real mechanism `sgs/brand-strip`'s wrapper-level padding/margin/border already uses (Spec 32 no-inline contract).
_meta.note_on_absorbs: `absorbs` (where present) lists OTHER setting-registry css rows that this member subsumes, so they need no member of their own. Used for the per-side box rows (css:padding-top/right/bottom/left, css:margin-*) which the shared BoxControl already covers via the merged `css:padding` / `css:margin` member. The FR-35-3 coverage validator counts an absorbed row as CLUSTERED — without this, the 8 per-side rows would be reported as false unclustered errors. Added 2026-07-20 (FR-35-2 merge case).
_meta.note_on_appliesToLayers: `appliesToLayers` (where present) scopes a member to elements at specific structural layers. It exists because ELEMENT is the PRIMARY mapping axis and cluster is SECONDARY: the 12 ARRANGEMENT members (display/flex-*/grid-*/justify-*/align-*/order/overflow) describe how an element arranges its CHILDREN, so they only apply to elements that HAVE children to arrange — layer OUTER or GRID. The 14 BOX members (padding/margin/gap/width/height/border-*/box-shadow/aspect-ratio) carry no appliesToLayers and apply to every element. NOTE `css:gap` is deliberately a BOX member, not arrangement: a leaf element legitimately has an internal gap (brand-strip's tile spaces its logo from its caption via logoGap). Tagging it as arrangement cost a real resolved member — caught and reverted 2026-07-20. Resolution rule: a member with appliesToLayers is checked ONLY when the element's `layer` is in that list. An un-layered element is never asked about arrangement members — the correct default, since it has not declared itself a structural layout layer. The earlier `isWrapper` fallback (removed from check-element-manifest-conformance.js:244-248) allowed un-layered elements to bypass this gate, causing 60 false gaps on buttons/quotes/media; all checked conformance now gates on element.layer exclusively.
_meta.note_on_layout_merge: The `flow` cluster (grid/flex arrangement) was merged INTO `layout` on 2026-07-20, reversing an earlier same-day split. Rationale (Bean): arrangement properties do control the layout of the items in a block, and the ELEMENT axis — not a second cluster — is what disambiguates 'size this box' from 'arrange these children'. role='layout' on a GRID element means arrangement; the same role on a tile/box element means sizing. One mechanism, not two. Element is the PRIMARY mapping axis (block_attributes.canonical_slot); cluster/role is SECONDARY.

states._note: Spec 35 FR-35-5 — the STATES axis. A state is a COMPONENT concept (hover/focus/selected/pressed/disabled); its CSS realisation is declared ONCE here, centrally, so no block re-derives it. States are DECLARED on a manifest element (never parsed from attribute names — see FR-35-5 'Why states are DECLARED, never parsed from names': tabActiveTextColour renders as [aria-selected="true"], NOT CSS :active, and pauseOnHover/effectHover/imageZoomHover/grayscaleHover contain 'Hover' but are booleans/preset selectors, not state-variant style properties).

hover.label: Hover
hover.note: Also emit :focus-visible where the control is focusable (a11y parity).

focus.label: Focus
focus.note: NOT bare :focus — avoids the mouse-click focus ring.

pressed.label: Pressed
pressed.note: Genuine mouse-down. Rare; distinct from selected.

members.label: Text colour (gradient)
members.note: Added 2026-08-16, gradient-rollout merge. Sibling to css:color the way css:background-image is sibling to css:background-color. Real CSS mechanism is background-image + background-clip:text (see sgs_text_colour_decl() in helpers-tokens.php) — deliberately NOT css:background-image itself, because that key is already claimed by the box-fill gradient (css:background-color's sibling) and a text element can legitimately have both a box background gradient and a text-fill gradient at once.

members.label: Text wrap
members.note: SGS-only — no nativeSupportsPath: no `typography.textWrap` (or any) key exists in WP core's block-supports typography vocabulary (verified via TypographyControls.js's own docblock, a full-tree search of `packages/` on WP 7.1). Currently 2 attrs: sgs/text.textWrap, sgs/heading.textWrap, both via the shared TypographyControls SelectControl. Draft addition pending Bean sign-off — see setting-registry-additions.json for the paired golden-master row.

members.label: Text columns
members.note: SGS-only — no nativeSupportsPath: core has no per-block `column-count` typography control (multi-column layout in core is the separate core/columns structural block, not a text-property control). Currently 1 attr: sgs/text.textColumns (NumberControl, 1-6), via the shared TypographyControls component. sgs/heading does NOT declare this attribute (verified by grep — heading's block.json has no textColumns-shaped key). Draft addition pending Bean sign-off — see setting-registry-additions.json for the paired golden-master row.

members.label: Line indent
members.note: SGS-only — no nativeSupportsPath: core has no `typography.textIndent` (or any) supports key; the paired UnitControl+RangeControl UI is a faithful reimplementation of core's own PRIVATE TextIndentControl (absent from @wordpress/block-editor's public components/index.js), including its 'Line indent' label and per-unit slider bounds. Currently 1 attr: sgs/text.textIndent, via the shared TypographyControls component. sgs/heading does NOT declare this attribute (verified by grep — heading's block.json has no textIndent-shaped key). Draft addition pending Bean sign-off — see setting-registry-additions.json for the paired golden-master row.

members.label: Opacity
members.note: Phase 0 item 0c, 2026-08-11 (D561): the last two widen an existing member rather than adding a css:* row — the same pattern 055a24ce used. sgs/container.backgroundMediaOpacity dims the ::before media layer (class-sgs-container-wrapper.php:727-730, D536); sgs/cta-section.backgroundImageOpacity dims that block's own hardcoded scrim (D536 names it as the LOOKALIKE of the former, not a duplicate). Both were falling through to tier-2 with nothing claiming them.

members.label: Stroke (SVG line paint)
members._note: Builder 4 (D636 gradient rollout, icon/SVG mechanism) — real attribute names, replacing D644's stopgap empty-suffix registration. Every SGS icon glyph (Lucide + the bundled @wordpress/icons subset) is stroke-based (`stroke="currentColor"` presentation attribute); a gradient can't ride the `color:`/currentColor chain a flat icon colour uses, so it paints instead via a real SVG <linearGradient>/<radialGradient> def + a `stroke:url(#id)` CSS override (helpers-svg-gradient.php). The sibling-attribute pattern names the gradient attr `{flatAttr}Gradient` (D636/D643 shape, matches every other builder this rollout) — hence the 4 suffixes here cover every real base/hover icon-colour attribute found across the framework (sgs/icon, sgs/icon-list, sgs/social-icons, sgs/business-info, sgs/button, sgs/cart, sgs/notice-banner, sgs/trust-bar, sgs/accordion). Resolution for these attrs is via EXPLICIT block.json attrMap (mirroring how css:color is already declared on every one of these elements), not suffix auto-derivation — this array exists to satisfy check-cluster-coverage.py's advisory coverage scan, per D644. Deliberately carries NO `appliesToLayers` (unlike css:fill's `["OUTER"]` restriction, copied then removed) — `memberAppliesToElement()` in check-element-manifest-conformance.js gates BASE-level resolution to elements whose declared `layer` is in that list, and every icon/glyph element this member targets is a leaf paint element, not an OUTER arrangement layer; leaving the restriction in produced 4 false ORPHAN:UNCLASSIFIED findings (icon/button/notice-banner/cart) with only the :hover state resolving (state resolution does not gate on appliesToLayers) — measured via `node scripts/check-element-manifest-conformance.js --check`, not assumed.

members.label: Fill (SVG paint, gradient)
members._note: Extends the D636 gradient rollout's SVG-gradient mechanism from stroke-based icon glyphs (css:stroke above) to FILL-based SVG shapes (star ratings — sgs/google-reviews, sgs/star-rating). Same helper, extended: `sgs_svg_stroke_gradient()` (helpers-svg-gradient.php) gained a third `$target` param ('stroke'|'fill') so it can emit `fill:url(#id)` instead of `stroke:url(#id)` for fill-based glyphs whose presentation attribute is `fill="…"` rather than `stroke="currentColor"`. Sibling-attribute naming is identical to css:stroke's (`{flatAttr}Gradient`). Resolution is via EXPLICIT block.json attrMap (mirroring css:fill's own attrMap entries on the same elements), not suffix auto-derivation — this array exists only to satisfy check-cluster-coverage.py's advisory coverage scan. Deliberately carries NO `appliesToLayers` for the same reason css:stroke omits it: every element this member targets (sgs/google-reviews `star`, sgs/star-rating `star`/`star-empty`) is a leaf paint element, not an OUTER arrangement layer — adding the restriction would reproduce css:stroke's own documented false-ORPHAN regression.

members.label: Background video source
members.note: Bean 2026-08-09: background media stays in the BACKGROUND section it already lives in. A <video> has no CSS property to name it; input:media-source already described it. BackgroundMedia added 2026-08-11 (Phase 0 item 0c, D561) for sgs/cta-section.backgroundMedia — one object attr accepting image OR video, so input:media-source describes it exactly. Deliberately NOT a new css:* row: check-cluster-coverage.py:12-25 records that a fabricated css:background-video would pass the gate while putting a lie in the golden master.

members.label: Background SVG source
members.note: Same ruling. Inline SVG markup, not a CSS property — input:code-svg's own label is 'Raw SVG markup (decorative background shape)'.

members.label: Height
members.note: ShapeDivider{Top,Bottom}Height deliberately NOT listed here. This member is unscoped (no appliesToLayers), and both `grid` and `wrapper` declare `layout`, so adding those suffixes made the divider heights claimable twice in 5 blocks — measured 2026-08-09: contested 9 -> 19. They need an OUTER-scoped home or an explicit attrMap entry, not a suffix on this member.

members.label: Border colour (gradient)
members.note: Added 2026-08-16, gradient-rollout merge (border builder). Sibling to css:border-color the way css:background-image is sibling to css:background-color. Real CSS mechanism is a masked ::before pseudo-element painting `background:<gradient>` clipped to a ring shape (see sgs_border_gradient_css() in helpers-tokens.php) — border-color itself can never legally hold a gradient in CSS. Deliberately its own member, not css:background-image, because an element can independently have a box-background gradient AND a border gradient at once.

members.label: Outline width
members.note: Added 2026-08-20. `outline` is a real, separately-painted CSS property — it is NOT border and NOT box-shadow. The framework paints focus rings with it (sgs/form style.css:207 `outline: var(--sgs-focus-ring-width) solid ...`). Before this member existed there was NO css:outline-* member of any kind, so a block mapping an attribute to css:outline-width referenced a member that did not exist and the attribute stayed an ORPHAN forever.

members.label: Outline offset
members.note: Added 2026-08-20 alongside css:outline-width. sgs/form style.css:209 `outline-offset: var(--sgs-focus-ring-offset)`.

members.label: Box shadow colour
members.note: Added 2026-08-20. Sibling to css:box-shadow exactly the way css:border-color-gradient is sibling to css:border-color. box-shadow is a COMPOUND property and its colour half is stored as its own attribute, set from the colour row rather than the shadow builder — Spec 35 PART O §1 field 9b names shadow colour as THE case for that split. It MUST be its own member and not another suffix on css:box-shadow, because a member claims exactly ONE attribute (the resolver returns on the first matching suffix), so the shadow VALUE attribute would always win and the colour would stay unclaimed. Before this member existed every {prefix}ShadowColour in the framework was unclaimable by construction, producing ORPHAN:STYLE-DEFECT findings on 6 blocks that were one shared model gap, not per-block defects.

members.label: Shape divider height
members.note: Bean 2026-08-09: divider heights sit at the bottom of the LAYOUT section. OUTER-scoped deliberately — routing these through the unscoped css:height member made them claimable by both `grid` and `wrapper` and took contested 9 -> 19 (measured, reverted).

members.label: Shape divider shape
members.note: Same ruling. The shape SELECTOR — a choice from a closed set, which is what input:enum-select describes.

animation.label: Animation
animation.owningComponent: ToggleGroupControl (preset picker) + RangeControl (ms unit) + ToggleGroupControl (easing presets)
